newsitem.title: BRAZIL: DM Grenfell says Brazil telecoms top LatAm picks.
newsitem.headline: DM Grenfell says Brazil telecoms top LatAm picks.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said Brazilian telecommunications stocks will be the top performing telecom shares in Latin America in 1997, followed by Telefonica del Peru and Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex).
The investment bank said in a report that the Brazilian economy's increasing liberalization will lead to greater operating flexibility and rate rebalancing for its mostly state telecoms.
"As a result, these companies should continue to show strong earnings growth and earnings growth in the medium term," it said.
Brazil's telecom sector, which is dominated by federal units, is set to be privatized in the next two years.

The bank said the moves toward liberalization and privatization are not reflected in the prices of Brazilian telecom stocks, which trade at discounts to other telecom stocks in the region as well as to Brazil's bolsas.
In 1997, Brazilian telecoms should benefit from further rate rebalancing at Telebras, competition in cellular services and progress on the privatization front, it said.

Its second choice, Telefonica del Peru, "operates within the most transparent and favorable regulatory environment in the region, with an independent regulator, a defined tariff structure and exclusivity until 1999," the bank said.
While Telefonica's stock trades at a premium to regional peers, it trades at a discount to the Peruvian bolsa and is sensitive to the changes in macroeconomic fundamentals, it said.
"As a result, Telefonica's share price should benefit from a turnaround in the economy and resolution of the hostage situation," the report said.
Telmex, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's No. 3 pick, will not be significantly affected by upcoming phased in competition in Mexico's telecom market, the bank said.
"We expect the stock to strengthen during the first half of the year with additional support coming from this year from a strong overall equity market in Mexico," it said.
Share prices could suffer after competition begins operating in 1997's second half, so "we recommend shifting to a neutral position in the stock by the second half of the year," the bank said.
